description: Key facts a correct lesson on each Engineering Graphics & Design topic must state. Every fact was taken from the fetched text of the source page named with it (the quote is checked by `npm run golden:check`). Patterns are case-insensitive regular expressions matched against the lesson text after LaTeX backslashes and braces are removed.
subject: engg-graphics

facts.claim: Orthographic projection: parallel projectors perpendicular to the plane

source.quote: all the projection lines are orthogonal to the projection plane

facts.claim: Represents a 3D object in 2D views

source.quote: is a means of representing three-dimensional objects in two dimensions

facts.claim: First-angle and third-angle projection

source.quote: The views are positioned relative to each other according to either of two schemes: first-angle or third-angle projection

facts.claim: In first-angle projection the object is in the first quadrant

source.quote: First-angle projection: In this type of projection, the object is imagined to be in the first quadrant

facts.claim: Front view (elevation), top view (plan) and side view

source.quote: These three views are known as front view (also elevation view), top view or plan view and end view

facts.claim: The three axes appear at 120° to each other

source.quote: the angle between any two of them is 120 degrees

facts.claim: Equal foreshortening on all three axes (equal measure)

source.quote: reflecting that the scale along each axis of the projection is the same

facts.claim: A conic is the locus where distance to focus ÷ distance to directrix = e

source.quote: whose distances to some particular point, called a focus, and some particular line, called a directrix, are in a fixed ratio, called the eccentricity

facts.claim: Ellipse, parabola and hyperbola (the circle is a special ellipse)

source.quote: There are three types of conics: the ellipse, parabola, and hyperbola

facts.claim: A cycloid is traced by a point on a circle rolling along a straight line

source.quote: a cycloid is the curve traced by a point on a circle as it rolls along a straight line without slipping

facts.claim: An involute is traced by the end of a taut string unwound from a circle

source.quote: the locus of a point on a piece of taut string as the string is either unwrapped from or wrapped around the curve

facts.claim: Gear teeth profiles are involutes of a circle

source.quote: The most common profiles of modern gear teeth are involutes of a circle

facts.claim: A vernier scale gives a finer reading between main-scale divisions

source.quote: a visual aid to take an accurate measurement reading between two graduation markings on a linear scale

facts.claim: e.g. 10 vernier divisions = 9 main-scale divisions

source.quote: has for instance ten divisions equal in distance to nine divisions on the main scale

facts.claim: Different line styles represent different features

source.quote: A variety of line styles graphically represent physical objects

facts.claim: Dimensions given once, with tolerances where needed

source.quote: Key information such as dimensions is usually only specified in one place on a drawing

facts.claim: Standards let everyone read a drawing the same way

source.quote: Standards provide rules for their specification and interpretation

facts.claim: An auxiliary plane parallel to an inclined surface shows its true shape

source.quote: By projecting into a plane parallel with the oblique surface, the true size and shape of the surface are shown

facts.claim: A development (net) unfolds the surface into a flat shape that folds back into the solid
facts.pattern: unfold|flat pattern|plane layout|laid out flat|fold(ed)? (up|back|along)|\bnet of (a|the) (solid|prism|cube|pyramid|cone|cylinder|polyhedron)|development of (the )?(lateral )?surfaces?

source.quote: an arrangement of non-overlapping edge-joined polygons in the plane that can be folded (along edges) to become the faces of the polyhedron

facts.claim: CAD uses computers to create, modify and analyse designs

source.quote: Computer-aided design (CAD) is the use of computers (or workstations) to aid in the creation, modification, analysis, or optimization of a design

facts.claim: CAD output still follows drawing conventions (dimensions, tolerances)

source.quote: the output of CAD must convey information, such as materials, processes, dimensions, and tolerances

facts.claim: Solid modelling represents complete 3D solids

source.quote: a consistent set of principles for mathematical and computer modeling of three-dimensional shapes (solids)

facts.claim: A section is where a cutting plane intersects a solid

source.quote: If a plane intersects a solid (a 3-dimensional object), then the region common to the plane and the solid is called a cross section of the solid

facts.claim: Sections show the internal arrangement of an object

source.quote: a common tool used to depict the internal arrangement of a 3-dimensional object in two dimensions

facts.claim: A line's true length appears only in a view parallel to it

source.quote: is the true length of the connector

facts.claim: Parallel projectors meet the plane of projection at right angles

source.quote: parallel projectors emanating from an imaginary object and intersecting an imaginary plane of projection at right angles
